doc.title: Arthur Davis and Andy Mosley Interview, 1960-01-12

title: Opening: names and work songs on the Angola radio station
summary: Arthur Davis is identified and asked what he does while singing; the room is explained as a prison radio station piping music to the dormitories, dated January 12, 1960.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Let's get your name down now, Arthur Davis. Arthur Davis? Yes sir. And you sing on this record, huh? Yes sir. And you're? And the Muslim. Mm-hmm. And you've got your lovers coming up too. So I thought we'd record a little bit of your impressions about it, and you can tell me about what the song means. Yes sir. What do you do? No, just let it go. What do you do when you sing this song? We'll all be in a group and sing a song, and practically after we get to the center, we'll rehearse on another one. But I mean, what kind of work are you supposed to be doing when you're singing? Well that's Phil, practically Phil work there. Con, Con, and Cut and Can. Well that's not you, let's skip this number. Okay?
Okay. I think you own this one.

That's Welch, I know that, huh? That's guitar there. Song And what is this call, this room here? This is a little station, south where we play our electric unit where we send it up to a different dormitory. This is a radio station? Yes sir. We have a hookup unit and a mic in each dormitory, going to dormitory 1 and dormitory 2. Oh yeah, I see. And a mic in the yard too, the fellas in the yard, and both can hear the music in three ways. And what's today's day? Let me get that down here. Today is January 12th, 1960. January 12th.
